entities.summary:
Jacopo Piccolomini-Ammannati was an Italian Renaissance cardinal and humanist who played a crucial role in the Catholic Church during the 15th century. Born into a noble family, Piccolomini studied at the University of Siena before being ordained as a priest.

As a prominent figure in the Papal Curia, Piccolomini was appointed Bishop of Pisa in 1456 and later became Cardinal-Bishop of Tusculum in 1462. He was a key advisor to several popes, including Pope Pius II and Pope Sixtus IV, and played a significant role in shaping the Church's policies during this period.

Despite his influential position, Piccolomini's personal life remains somewhat mysterious. His exact date of birth is unknown, but he died on September 19, 1479. He was buried in the Basilica of Santa Maria sopra Minerva in Rome.

In addition to his ecclesiastical duties, Piccolomini was a patron of the arts and architecture. He commissioned several notable buildings and monuments during his lifetime, including the Piccolomini Library at the Siena Cathedral.

Piccolomini's legacy extends beyond his own time period, as he played a significant role in shaping the course of European history. His influence can be seen in the artistic and architectural developments of the Renaissance era, which had far-reaching consequences for Western culture.

The famous phrase 'Tempora mutantur, nos et mutamur in illis' ('Times change, we change with them') attributed to Piccolomini highlights his pragmatic approach to dealing with the changing world around him. This phrase has become a timeless reminder of the importance of adaptability and resilience in the face of uncertainty.

Piccolomini's life serves as a testament to the enduring power of human ingenuity, creativity, and perseverance. Despite facing numerous challenges and setbacks throughout his life, he remained committed to his values and vision, leaving behind a lasting legacy that continues to inspire people around the world today.
